events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author on 14 August 2026; also concerns Borsuk's partition problem, a different problem (F15).
events.ai_basis: The example and proof were generated entirely by ChatGPT using GPT 5.6 Sol.
In May 2026, Max Grinsztajn, assisted by OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Pro, lowered the minimum known failing dimension to 63

why: The statement is a single universal claim, so a counterexample in any dimension refutes it outright; the Bryant–Ferry n ≥ 6 counterexamples are therefore scored whole/refuted/counterexample, but both their announcement (March 2018) and the written preprint (in existence by 30 December 2023 per Valov) predate the snapshot, and they remain unreviewed (cited and reported by Valov, not verified), so they tier only as a pre-snapshot claim. Bing–Borsuk 1965 settles n = 1, 2 (case, digested). Jakobsche, BFMW and Valov's dimension-theoretic papers prove no manifold conclusion (none); Bryant 2006 and Valov 2016/2025 address homology or other Bing–Borsuk questions (variant). The only in-window event on the topic, Fujioka–Gu, proves manifoldness for Busemann G-spaces with convex balls, with no established finite dimension or ANR status, so it is a variant rather than a case. Ji and Grinsztajn concern Borsuk's partition problem, a different problem (F15), and are variants; their AI roles are recorded from their own quotes but cannot touch this statement.
doubts: Close call on the Bryant–Ferry scope: a per-dimension reading would make it a case (n ≥ 6) rather than whole; either way it is pre-snapshot and unreviewed, so it does not affect the post-2024 count. Its written version's first posting date is only bounded above by December 2023; if it was in fact first posted after 26 January 2024 the conclusion would change, but the record shows Valov citing a revised version on 30 December 2023. The Grinsztajn AI attribution rests on Wikipedia, not the author's own account.
